Humpty Dumpty in Irish and English

In Irish it is Humpty Dumpty. Here are the words in both languages, side by side, with a gentle tune to sing along to.

Sing along in Irish Sing along in English

The words light up as the tune plays. No microphone, nothing to sign up for.

Humpty Dumpty (Irish)

Humpty Dumpty thuas ar an mballa,
Humpty Dumpty thit sé le plab.
Caipill an rí is fir an rí go léir, níor
chuir siad Humpty Dumpty ar ais le chéile.

Humpty Dumpty (English)

Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall,
Humpty Dumpty had a great fall.
All the king's horses and all the king's men couldn't
put Humpty Dumpty together again.

About the song

Words: traditional, first printed 1797. Tune: as printed in Our Old Nursery Rhymes (Alfred Moffat, 1911), read from the Project Gutenberg MusicXML. Public domain.

The Irish words were written for Calm Match to fit the same tune, one syllable to each note. They are still being checked by a fluent Irish speaker, so they may change. Spotted something to improve? Email hello@calmmatch.com.
